Students are expected to develop a general knowledge of the history, theory, and methodology of ethnomusicology or systematic musicology, and to gain experience in ethnographic fieldwork and musical performance (for those in the ethnomusicology concentration) or in scientific and philosophical methods (for those in the systematic musicology concentration).

description: The Department of Ethnomusicology offers the Master of Arts (M.A.) and Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degrees in Ethnomusicology. The graduate program in Ethnomusicology is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the history, theory, and practice of the field. Students learn to conduct original research on musical traditions from around the world, using a variety of methods including ethnographic fieldwork, archival research, and musical analysis. The program is one of the oldest and largest in the world, with a faculty that includes leading scholars in the field and a student body drawn from across the globe. The Ph.D. in ethnomusicology provides students with the tools to conduct original research on music as a cultural and social phenomenon. Students work closely with faculty members to develop their research projects, which often involve extensive fieldwork and archival research. The program emphasizes both theoretical rigor and practical skills, preparing students for careers in academia, public sector work, and the arts. Students in the Ph.D. program in Ethnomusicology are expected to develop a high level of expertise in at least one musical tradition and to gain a broad understanding of the field as a whole. The program also offers students the opportunity to participate in performance ensembles, which provide hands-on experience in a variety of musical traditions. Graduate students in Ethnomusicology may also elect to complete a specialization in Systematic Musicology.

description: The Master of Music and Doctor of Musical Arts degrees provide students with a high level of professional training in their specific performance area. These programs focus on the development of artistic maturity, technical mastery, and a broad knowledge of the repertoire. Students are encouraged to pursue their own artistic and professional goals through a flexible curriculum that includes private instruction, ensemble participation, and a variety of elective courses in musicology, ethnomusicology, and music education.

The UCLA Department of Musicology offers programs of study leading to the Master of Arts and Doctor of Philosophy degrees. The department is a community of scholars and students whose work explores a wide range of musical practices, from Western classical music to popular music, jazz, and music of the world’s cultures. Our faculty and students are committed to interdisciplinary approaches to music, drawing on perspectives from history, cultural studies, gender and sexuality studies, ethnic studies, and media studies. The M.A. and Ph.D. programs in musicology are intended for students who want to combine a deep knowledge of music with a broad understanding of its social and cultural contexts. The department is known for its pioneering role in the development of 'new musicology,' which emphasizes the study of music in relation to issues of gender, sexuality, race, and politics.

description: The Ph.D. program in Musicology at UCLA is one of the nation’s most distinguished programs of its kind. Our graduates have a high rate of success in securing academic positions and winning prestigious fellowships.

This core training is intended to provide the necessary tools for research in history, religious studies, archaeology, and other fields in the humanities and social sciences. description: The Neuroscience Ph.D. Program is a member of the Graduate Programs in Bioscience (GPB) which is an umbrella organization of 11 Ph.D. programs. Students apply to the program through the Graduate Programs in Bioscience. All students who are admitted to the Neuroscience Ph.D. Program are fully supported. During the first year, students take courses in the core curriculum and complete three laboratory rotations. At the end of the first year, students choose a research mentor and join a laboratory. Neuroscience students can choose from over 150 faculty mentors. Research in Neuroscience at UCLA is very broad, and the Neuroscience Ph.D. program allows students to pursue research in many different areas. These include: molecular, cellular, and developmental neuroscience; systems neuroscience; and behavioral and cognitive neuroscience.

Concentration name: Master’s Entry Clinical Nurse (MECN), Advanced Practice Registered Nurse (APRN) (Specialties: Adult/Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner, Adult/Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner, Family Nurse Practitioner, Pediatric Nurse Practitioner Primary Care, Pediatric Nurse Practitioner Acute Care)
description: The UCLA School of Nursing offers a Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) degree to two groups of students: those with a natural science or social science degree in another field who want to become a registered nurse (MECN) and those who have a BSN degree and want to become an advanced practice nurse (APRN). The MECN program is a two-year pre-licensure program designed for students with a bachelor’s degree in a non-nursing field, preparing them for the NCLEX-RN and clinical leadership. The APRN program is designed for registered nurses with a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) who wish to prepare for roles as Nurse Practitioners or Clinical Nurse Specialists in specific populations.
Accreditation status: The master's degree program in nursing at the UCLA School of Nursing is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE).

description: The PhD program in the School of Nursing at UCLA is designed to prepare scientists who will conduct research to improve the health of individuals and populations and to prepare nurse educators for the role of faculty. Research is the core of the program and builds on the strong clinical and research backgrounds of our faculty. The PhD program offers a curriculum that builds on previous knowledge and experience, provides a foundation in nursing science and research methodology, and allows for the pursuit of individual research interests.

Program Page url: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu/).

Program Page url: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu/).

description: The UCLA Master of Quantitative Economics (MQE) is a STEM-certified program designed for students who want to become experts at analyzing data and solving complex problems in the global economy. In today’s data-driven world, economists need to be able to use data to tell a story and provide insights that lead to better decision-making. The MQE program provides students with the tools they need to succeed in a variety of careers, including finance, consulting, and data science. Our world-renowned faculty teach students how to apply economic theory to real-world problems. We also offer a variety of professional development opportunities, including internships and career coaching. If you are looking for a program that will challenge you and prepare you for a successful career in economics, the UCLA MQE program is the right choice for you.

The UCLA Scandinavian Section offers a program of graduate study leading to the M.A. and Ph.D. in Scandinavian. Field education serves as the “signature pedagogy” of the program, offering an intensive, supervised learning experience where students transition from the classroom to becoming practitioners in the community. During their field placements, students apply the theories and skills they learn in the classroom to real-world settings under the guidance of experienced social work professionals.

description: Social welfare at UCLA Luskin is a diverse and multidisciplinary field that examines how we can meet the needs of all members of society, particularly those who are marginalized or vulnerable. Our curriculum covers diverse research areas, including health and behavioral health, aging, children and families, globalization and social justice, mental health, and more. Through a combination of rigorous coursework, independent research, and mentorship from world-renowned faculty, students will develop the skills and expertise needed to become leaders in the field and to create positive social change. If you’re ready to take the next step in your academic journey and make a real-world impact, we invite you to explore the PhD in Social Welfare at UCLA Luskin.

description: The Graduate Certificate in Food Studies is designed to provide UCLA graduate students with a multidisciplinary perspective on the impact of food on people and the planet. The 12-to-20-unit certificate program, based at UCLA Fielding but open to any UCLA graduate student, provides a common ground for students from a wide range of disciplines to come together and think critically about food’s impact on people and the planet. It allows students to engage with their peers from around the campus to learn how their specific field can contribute to addressing food-related issues, as well as how other fields are approaching them. The core courses examine food from both the perspective of human health and the environmental impact. In addition to the core courses, students choose elective courses from a wide range of fields, which can include public health, medicine, management, law, history, geography, anthropology, public policy, urban planning, and environment and sustainability.

UCLA’s Urban Humanities Initiative (UHI) is a program of research and study that brings together the humanities, architecture and urban design, and urban planning. Funded by the Andrew W. Mellon Foundation, UHI provides graduate students with the opportunity to earn a Graduate Certificate in Urban Humanities by participating in a sequence of core courses, seminars, and studios that address the complex issues of the global city.

The Graduate Certificate in Writing Pedagogy provides a structured environment for UCLA graduate students to develop a specialization in the theory and practice of teaching writing at the college level. The program is designed to integrate pedagogical development with students’ ongoing graduate coursework and research, emphasizing the connection between writing, learning, and disciplinary knowledge. To earn the certificate, students must complete the following requirements: 1. Two courses in writing pedagogy: Students must take English 495A (Pedagogy of Writing) or an equivalent departmental course in the pedagogy of writing. They must also take one additional 4-unit course on writing pedagogy. 2. Teaching experience: Students must have at least two quarters of experience teaching writing-intensive courses at UCLA. 3. Pedagogy workshops: Students must participate in at least two pedagogy workshops offered by Writing Programs or other campus units. 4. Teaching Portfolio: Students must submit a portfolio that includes a statement of teaching philosophy, sample syllabi, and other evidence of teaching effectiveness.

The Global Health Certificate is an interdisciplinary program for graduate students at UCLA. The program is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the major issues in global health and to equip them with the knowledge and skills necessary to address these challenges. The certificate is open to all UCLA graduate and professional students.

The Bixby Certificate in Population and Reproductive Health provides UCLA Fielding School of Public Health students with a deeper understanding of the factors that influence the health of populations, with a focus on reproductive health and rights. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in reproductive health, family planning, and population dynamics, both domestically and internationally. Students gain skills in demographic methods, program evaluation, and policy analysis. To receive the Bixby Certificate, students must complete: a minimum of 16 units of coursework in population and reproductive health; a 400-hour field experience in a population or reproductive health-related organization; and a culminating project (e.g., master’s report, thesis, or dissertation) on a population or reproductive health topic.

description: The Leaders in Sustainability (LiS) graduate certificate program is designed for UCLA graduate students (masters and doctoral) who want to add a sustainability lens to their primary field of study. Students from any UCLA graduate or professional school are eligible to participate. The program allows students to work with graduate students from different backgrounds, participate in sustainability-related leadership and professional development, and complete a sustainability-focused capstone project.
